title: Rear Brake Caliper Anchor Plate Removal and Installation
introduction:
The anchor plate carries the brake pads beside the disc while the caliper supplies the squeeze. Think of it as the shelf bracket behind the friction business: less glamorous than the caliper, but essential to keeping everything in place.

This procedure applies to the supplied rear-disc-brake arrangements for the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines. I use the drawing to distinguish the blue anchor plate from its magenta mounting bolts; the disposal symbol means those bolts must be replaced. Wheel removal and the linked brake-pad procedure provide access, and their installation details remain part of finishing this job.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Before working around or underneath the vehicle, disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could start remotely and cause personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting it during service; an accidental start can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Protection and materials
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts; failure to do so can cause serious personal injury. Read the material safety information before using the specified chemicals or materials, because improper use can cause serious personal injury. If using solvents for cleaning, keep them away from ignition sources: they can ignite or explode and cause serious personal injury. Review the applicable [general service warnings](#/document/G1693189), [brake precautions](#/document/G1693183) and [wheel precautions](#/document/G1693193) before starting.

items.name: Underhood reservoir access
items.detail: Before the underhood fluid check, inspect cooling fans with the ignition OFF for damage, cracks or separation. Do not work under the hood with a damaged fan; replace it with a new fan first, because it can separate during operation and cause serious personal injury. Fans can run with the ignition off. The requirement to disable them applies before work near a fan; this reservoir-level check is not an instruction to work on or reach into a fan assembly. If your access would place you near a fan, stop and obtain the applicable isolation procedure before continuing.

requirements.category: Lift safely and gain wheel access

items.name: Use the prescribed hoist setup
items.detail: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on a hoist as required by [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). Confirm the hoist can carry the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. Use the lift-arm positions in [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631), identifying the correct points by the triangles stamped into the body or frame. Incorrect lifting locations can let the vehicle shift or fall and cause serious personal injury. Incorrect hoist-arm positioning can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death. Do not use the engine to power the drive wheels unless all drive wheels are clear of the ground.

items.name: Protect the vehicle during lifting
items.detail: Position hoist adapters clear of the suspension, exhaust and steering linkage. On a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped, and avoid damaging the axle or rear cover. Before driving onto a drive-on lift, check for underbody interference. Do not apply jack pressure to either bumper; it will damage the covers. The vehicle's emergency jack is for changing a deflated tire, not this repair. Never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; it can lower unexpectedly. Use floor stands whenever a jack supports the vehicle, or serious personal injury can result.

items.name: Remove the wheel without adding damage
items.detail: Remove the wheel nuts and take off the wheel and tire using the linked wheel procedure. Do not heat a seized wheel nut; heat can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. If the wheel is cracked, deflate the tire before removing the wheel from the vehicle; a cracked wheel can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Control friction dust
items.detail: Do not breathe brake dust or blow it from friction components or storage containers with compressed air. Remove it using government-approved techniques. Friction dust can present cancer and lung-disease hazards, irritate skin, eyes and the respiratory tract, cause allergic reactions and lead to other chronic health effects. Seek medical attention or advice if irritation persists. Failure to observe these precautions can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Support the caliper
items.detail: Have a support ready before moving the caliper aside. The brake-pad illustration shows a support hook. Keep the caliper's weight off the brake hose throughout removal and installation; the hose must not serve as a suspension strap.

items.name: Conditional piston retraction
items.detail: If installing new brake pads, use a Brake Caliper Piston Retractor to retract the pistons into the caliper bore. Apply moderate to heavy force toward the piston: without sufficient force, the internal park brake mechanism clutch cone will not engage and the piston will not compress. Before installing the caliper, align the piston notch with the pin on the inboard pad. These details belong to the linked [Brake Pads](#/document/G1693756) procedure; piston retraction is conditional on installing new pads.

items.name: Keep brake fluid clean
items.detail: For any required top-up, use only clean Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2 as listed in [Specifications](#/document/G1694687). Never reuse drained fluid. These precautions prevent system contamination, component damage and the risk of serious personal injury. Immediately wash any brake-fluid spill on paintwork with cold water.

items.name: Restore the pad and caliper assembly
items.detail: After fastening the anchor plate with new mounting bolts, reverse the linked pad-removal sequence: refit the clips and pads, then return the supported caliper to position, observing the piston-notch and inboard-pad-pin alignment requirement. Tighten the caliper bolts to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm). These are the caliper bolts, distinct from the anchor-plate bolts.

items.name: Prepare the wheel mounting surfaces
items.detail: Before refitting the wheel, remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel mounting surface and the mating hub or brake-disc surface. Make sure any rotor-to-hub fasteners are secured clear of those mounting surfaces. Otherwise, the wheel nuts can loosen and the wheel can come off in motion, causing loss of control, serious injury or death. Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, specified in [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) only at the wheel-pilot-bore and hub-pilot interface. Keep it off the wheel-to-disc mounting faces, studs, nuts, pads and disc friction surfaces to prevent component damage.

items.name: Complete wheel installation first
items.detail: Position the wheel and install its nuts finger tight initially. With the vehicle resting on its tires, finish tightening in the illustrated star/cross pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), using clean, dry stud and nut threads. Skipping the pattern can produce high disc runout and accelerate brake roughness, shudder and vibration. Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi), because wheels can loosen after initial tightening and cause serious injury.

items.name: Then complete the brake-fluid check
items.detail: After reversing removal completely, including wheel installation, depress the brake pedal. Then check the reservoir fluid level and top up as necessary using Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2 in [Specifications](#/document/G1694687). This is the completion order required by [Brake Pads](#/document/G1693756).

items.name: Home-garage preparation
items.detail: Do not judge asbestos content by appearance. EPA suggests professional servicing when the material is uncertain. If that is not possible and professional dust-control equipment is unavailable, its home-mechanic guidance describes wet wiping: use a low-pressure fine mist of water or detergent-amended water to wet the brake parts, then wipe them with a cloth. Keep bystanders, food and drinks away.

items.name: Contain dust and waste
items.detail: Do not blow dust with compressed air or clean it with a dry rag, brush or garden hose. Do not use an ordinary vacuum lacking HEPA filtration. Keep contaminated clothing and dust out of the house; change clothes and wash soiled clothing separately. EPA recommends double-bagging asbestos waste and following local disposal rules. Read the full [EPA brake-and-clutch guidance](https://www.epa.gov/asbestos/current-best-practices-preventing-asbestos-exposure-among-brake-and-clutch-repair-0) before starting.

items.name: Keep the instructions distinct
items.detail: This is EPA guidance for home mechanics, not a claim that every brake contains asbestos or that employer OSHA duties apply to your home garage.

items.name: Control the transition onto and off the hoist
items.detail: Keep the vehicle restrained with the parking brake and ground-wheel restraints while positioning it for lifting. Establish that every wheel is fully clear of the ground and the vehicle is securely supported on the prescribed hoist before releasing the parking brake for rear-caliper work. After the caliper, pads and all parking-brake components disturbed for access are fully refitted, reapply the parking brake before lowering. Restore ground-wheel restraints as the tires meet the ground, before final wheel-nut tightening.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps for installation details as well; some refitting instructions appear alongside removal.
edits.why: The mounting-bolt replacement rule and tightening specification must be carried forward into reassembly.

edits.text:
Remove the brake pads using Brake Pads (206-04 Rear Disc Brake, Removal and Installation).
Refer to: [Brake Pads](#/document/G1693756).
edits.why: After removing the wheel and tire, support the caliper, remove its mounting bolts and position it aside without loading the brake hose. Remove the brake pads, then their clips. Clearing those parts exposes the anchor plate; keep the caliper supported while the plate is removed. The caliper bolts are refitted to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm), distinct from the new anchor-plate bolts specified below. See [Brake Pads](#/document/G1693756) for the source procedure.

edits.text: NOTICE: Support the brake caliper and anchor plate assembly. Do not let it hang from the brake hose; its weight can damage the hose.
edits.why: The hose carries brake fluid, not the weight of loose brake hardware. Maintain support as the fasteners come out and the components move.

edits.text: Remove the 2 bolts and take off the brake caliper anchor plate. Discard the removed bolts. During installation, use new bolts and tighten them to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm).
edits.why: The drawing highlights the anchor plate in blue and its mounting bolts in magenta. The disposal callout identifies the fasteners that cannot be reused; the torque shown here is their installation torque.

edits.text: Install by reversing the removal procedure, using new anchor-plate bolts and the installation details given above.
edits.why: Refit the anchor plate before restoring the clips, pads and caliper through the linked Brake Pads procedure. Observe its piston-alignment requirement and its conditional retraction instructions if fitting new pads. Complete wheel installation, including final wheel-nut tightening with the vehicle resting on its tires, before depressing the brake pedal and checking and topping up the reservoir. The linked Specifications reference identifies the required brake fluid.
